item.title: SCP draft- Ancient Nautiloids
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: Due to the various populations of SCP-XXXX being spread out in the Atlantic Ocean, SCP-XXXX instances are to be monitored by multiple research vessels. Only personnel with a marine biology background or naval background are allowed to monitor SCP-XXXX instances.

ROVs or dive crews are permitted to observe SCP-XXXX instances. Dive teams must keep a distance of 5-10 when approaching. If the observing instance of SCP-XXXX shows no interest to personnel, personnel shouldn’t attempt to follow or surrounding SCP-XXXX instances will flee.

Should eggs be discovered, divers or ROVs should be sent on a monthly basis to monitor the egg depending on the depth of the water. Monitoring should end when all eggs are hatched. Unhatched eggs are to be collected for observation.

Washed-up carcasses or shells of SCP-XXXX instances must be removed from the location discovered. Any person of the public must be treated with amnestics after the confiscation of items. Info of the SCP from outside researchers and media must be confiscated immediately to prevent public curiosity. A cover story must be formed after doing so.

If the ritual battle of SCP-XXXX instances would occur, ships controlled by the foundation must set up a perimeter of a radius of 10 kilometers around the center of the Bermuda Triangle. The perimeter can only disperse when the battle is over and the lone instance of SCP-XXXX has left.

Description: SCP-5181 is a designation of 4 species of nautiloids located around the world. They are designated as SCP-XXXX-A to D. Each one is vastly different from the other.

SCP-XXXX-A are conical-shelled nautiloids with a shell length of 4 meters. Resembling an Orthoceras in physique, SCP-XXXX-A’s arms are 1.5 meters long. The skin of this instance is maroon. The color of the shell is a dark shade of brown with orange stripes.

SCP-XXXX-A are migratory in nature. They live in the North Atlantic for the summers before heading south in the fall. Instances of SCP-XXXX-A return to the north in mid-April.

SCP-XXXX-B are curved-shelled nautiloids with a shell length of 1.5 meters. At a meter up the shell, a blade-like protrusion is apparent that starts 20cm from the shel’s basel. Arms of this instance are hooked and 70cm long each. A thin line of webbing about 20cm from the base is present on SCP-XXXX-B. The shell protrusion is sharp enough to slice prey when the instance SCP-XXXX-B rams into it.

Instances of SCP-XXXX-B are observed to live in the open waters in the Caribbean Sea. From observation, SCP-XXXX-B rams itself into schools of fish. Fish are either cut by the protrusion or incapacitated by the shell.

SCP-XXXX-C are nautiloids 1 meter in diameter resembling a chambered nautilus in physique. The shell is a charcoal grey coloring with grooves where the walls of the chambers are located. Its skin coloring is primarily navy blue. Instances of SCP-XXXX-C are capable of emitting cyan-colored bioluminescence at the ends of their tentacles.

SCP-XXX-C live in benthic environments near submarine canyons of the Atlantic ocean that lead to open waters. SCP-XXXX-C will outstretch its arms radially and emit its bioluminescence. Prey is hypnotized and is compelled to come close. From there, SCP-XXXX-C will wrap its tentacles around the prey before consuming.

SCP-XXXX-D are coiled-shelled nautiloids that are approximately shell diameter of 2 meters. The shell is a gradient of orange and yellow with a black stone-like outer layer. The pattern of the shell is supposed to resemble cooling lava. Arms are 5 meters long from the base to the tip. All tentacles have microscopic hairs on them. This suggests instances of SCP-XXXX-D can feed similar to yeti crabs.

SCP-XXXX-D instances are seen near hydrothermal vents off in the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. The instances of SCP-XXXX-D are very slow-moving due to the weight of the shell. Though capable of catching prey, it prefers to harvest bacteria for chemosynthesis. After the synthesis is sufficient, it will eat the bacteria.

All instances of SCP-XXXX reach sexual maturity at around 10 years. Each female instance lays a clutch of 10-30 eggs. The eggs are hard and soft as leather. Gestation period of the eggs is about 10-12 months. Once hatched, instances of SCP-XXXX will have a yolk to survive on for the first two weeks of life. Hatchlings look like miniature versions of their adult forms. A small yolk is present when the instances are born. After two weeks, the yolk is used up and the offspring are ready to hunt for themselves.

Every 10 years in around mid to late April, at least one instance of each instance of SCP-XXXX will meet at the center of the Bermuda Triangle. Once all of the instances are gathered, they all fight to the death. The fight will only end after there’s a sole survivor of the death match. The sole survivor will leave the battle to return to its home.

After the battle the population of the instance significantly grows for the next three years. The boom in population of the winning instance is likely due to the instances of SCP-XXXX reaching sexual maturity at the same amount of time. It’s theorized that the battles are some kind of ritual for fertility rights.

Discovery
Instances of SCP-XXXX were discovered in April 2005 by an international oceanography survey. On sonar, they discovered four blips near the center of the Bermuda Triangle. The survey team stopped at about a kilometer to not spook what creatures were there. Divers are sent after the ships stopped moving.

According to the divers witnessing the event, there was at least one individual of each SCP-XXXX instance. All of the instances were attacking each other disregarding their own wellbeing. After the battle, only the instance of SCP-XXXX-B left the battle alive, albeit barely.

After testimonies of the crew were given, amnestics were administered to them. Footage and logs of SCP-XXXX were confiscated and destroyed after copying data to the foundation database.

Addendum XXXX-1
After analyzing the shells, only the shells of SCP-XXXX-B and SCP-XXXX-D have abnormalities. Traces of Iron are found where the protrusion SCP-XXXX-B. The protrusion itself is about 85% iron.

The rock growths on SCP-XXXX-D’s shell have properties of pumice but of unknown composition. It is theorized that the pumice-like rocks help with SCP-XXXX-D to maintain buoyancy.

Addendum XXXX-2
The captivity of SCP-XXXX instances is impossible at this point in time. All instances have died during transport or within hours of being settled in a theoretically suitable enclosure.

Addendum XXXX-3
On April 20, 2015, another battle among the SCP-XXXX instances occurred. The weather at the time was mostly cloudy with high winds. Monitoring of the battle was difficult due to the rising waves. The instance of SCP-XXXX-D was declared the victor by the foundation after the shells of the other instances were discovered.

item.title: Re: Data not redacted? (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
My apologies for the delay in responding.

I would largely second cybersqyd's suggestions here. There is a lacking sense of stakes and motivation, and whilst hinting at things and not being explicit can be appropriate at times, it can also leave the overall narrative feeling unsatisfying or lacking in motivation.

Creating an interactive tale is something I would not advise here - integrating the EC/O5 interplay into a single SCP article would not be too much for one article and would give this article the necessary narrative momentum and intrigue to pay-off on the premise appropriately - putting it into an interactive tale would strip the initial article of the necessary narrative heft whilst presenting you with the challenge of creating an interactive tale (which is amongst the most difficult things you can try to do on the site, in my opinion).

The primary problem here is that you've got a premise that is a little derivative of other pieces on the site, and without a narrative to really differentiate itself, it's going to come across as unoriginal and stale. The idea of an EC/O5 interplay is a good one and could create some interesting insight into the internal politics of the Foundation and the conflicting factions therein, but without it, you're going to have a rather meandering narrative that won't really explore the premise or its place in the universe well enough to be interesting, in my opinion. Another narrative could do that, but the primary thing you've got here about discovery and researching theories isn't going to do that because it's simply exploring what the anomaly is rather than how it interacts with the world it inhabits.

item.title: Re: Differences between MTF Omega-7 and MTF Alpha-9
item.content:encoded:
Omega-7 was a much earlier version of the team that was disbanded after SCP-076 (who was a member) went berserk and an entire Site was nuked to stop him. I know you said you didn't want to read details, but the story is here. It's a lot shorter than the Alpha-9 stuff.

Alpha-9 comes from the Resurrection canon, where the idea of an anomalous humanoid SCP MTF was, well, resurrected. SCP-105 is the only member of Omega-7 who is also in Alpha-9. I don't know the current state of the Resurrection canon, but I'm pretty sure they aren't actually fully approved and in action in that canon.

A word to the wise: Outside of the fiction, most SCPs that were in Omega-7 or were written to be in Omega-7 were deleted due to low quality. If you're thinking about writing a humanoid SCP into an MTF, be careful, you're heading into rough waters.

Honestly, most of the anomalous humanoids I know of in MTFs have their own specific MTFs instead of being in Alpha-9, and even then you still need to justify it. For example, Tau-5 sees a lot of use beyond their original stories, whereas I'm pretty sure Alpha-9 is only talked about in that particular canon.

item.title: Mean Grannie
item.content:encoded:
I loved this one, especially with the included log of the containment breach.
I also enjoy all the comments asking "well, what if all the people who interacted with it really were bad, and it just needs to meet someone nice"? Personally, I think that it's just an awful entity, and part of the awfulness is getting the victims - or in this case the readers - to somehow think this hideous fate is deserved. It's the abuser saying "now look what you made me do".
To be sure, you could test the "punish the wicked" theory using someone who is almost guaranteed to be good, like a child. But if you're wrong, it would be monstrous.
I love SCPs that don't wrap everything up nicely but leave some unsolved questions.

item.title: Null tower
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX Is a spiral stairwell underneath a lighthouse located outside of Koror, Palau. The stairwell contains writings written with plantlife in an unknown language. Anybody can read it, but no cognitohazards have been identified.
Near the bottom of the stairwell is an entity observed to write the text on the walls. It has an appearance similar to a wendigo glowing a bright white color. people to entity as "the Null walker" when never given its name. It's docile but can cause illusions to provokers.
At the bottom of the stairwell is a bioluminescent cave with more text and unidentified life.

Central Narrative: In the first exploration, a D-Class was to record the texts and descend as low as he can. He was able to find the Null walker, but what happened next was unknown.
In the second exploration log, a 3 man MTF team was to continue exploration with better equipment. 5 hours in, the leader of the MTF goes into the stairwell alone and tells nobody to follow him. After 30 minutes, he is found to have committed suicide by gunshot, with a note saying that the Null walker will reincarnate him and keep him from harm. The next day he was found continuing his daily routine, with no recollection of the event.
A 4 person MTF team was to have a more permanent exploration in the final exploration log. A Cognito hazard specialist, Linguistic, Anomalous biologist, and a psychologist were sent. The cognitohazard specialist and the linguist went missing, and later the linguist was found dead and killed by the Cognitohazard specialist (who is missing). The biologist and the psychologist team up and cut off the connection to control. One month later, they are also found in their daily routine with no recollection of the event.
In the end, they find journals belonging to the biologist and previous MTFs. In the biologist's journal, she talks about how she and the psychologist looked out for each other and how they killed the cognitohazard specialist. After they went down to the bottom of the stairwell and found the giant bioluminescent cave and the D-classes' animated bodies and the previous MTF, were glowing blue and showed no intelligence.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP gives an urge for both the foundation and the readers to find out what is at the bottom of the stairwell.

Additional Notes: 400-word limit, ask questions so I answer

item.title: My Eternal Crusade
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An indestructible and immortal crusader is on a quest to rid the world of SCP's either by killing them or cleansing them of their "corruption."

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: An MTF Squad is out looking for an SCP that had escaped containment, but instead end up finding the Crusader after having just killed it. They take him into custody, and quickly realize just what they have found and make a deal with him. Discovering unlike other SCP's, once you take away his "blessed" weapons and shield he's just your everyday, immortal, above average human male wearing crusader armor, the Foundation makes him an offer. He begrudgingly agrees and helps the Foundation to capture or kill dangerous SCP’s. Twice, when sent on a mission to capture a new SCP, the Crusader disobeys orders, killing one SCP but helping another escape before letting either one be identified. The second time becomes the last straw, and when questioned, it becomes apparent that up to this point all that mattered was his quest, but this is a much more personal matter that he refuses to share with the Foundation. The only things he ends up telling the Foundation is that many others also believed the knowledge they would gain would outweigh the danger, and that not all birds were meant to be caged.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Foundation is always seeking anti anomalous SCP's to help contain other SCP's or put down dangerous ones. But are they willing to compromise and negotiate to achieve that goal? Would they set aside their own beliefs, ideals, and processes for ultimately the greater good, or choose to lose such an asset for the sake of doing things their way? At what point, will they refuse to compromise any further?

Additional Notes: While I’m a fast learner, I don’t have the time or the will to go through every SCP Article, Tale, and Group of Interest. If something here has already been done, or is too similar to something else please let me know.

item.title: Re: Chearleader Pom Poms[Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
[Summoned via PM]

Hi there! Disclaimer I'm not a veteran reviewer and I'm unable to provide Greenlights. Without further ado…

Lets take a look at this.
-

It looks like I will be echoing the same points as Dr Sage Evergreen because I like this a lot. I am a big fan of emotional articles like this, and I think this is a very well thought out idea. The most important thing to keep in mind with this article will be execution. Like cybersqyd said, you will need to be careful that you do not give away the ending too early on. You could solve this with Dr Sage Evergreen's idea, and a good example of an article that tells a story in this way would be SCP-5866. It is told from a viewpoint of an article that is in the process of being written. You could do something similar to this, perhaps having a separate researcher re editing the file in order to fix his mistakes, and slowly finding out what happened through the course of the edits. I honestly wish I could greenlight this, but sadly I can't. That is why I recommend going over to the IRC chatrom, and going over to #thecritters. You can post a link to your forum page there, and this will help you find your final greenlight.

To summarize, I like this idea a lot, and I wish you luck going forward. I hope I see this in the Draft Forum soon.

item.title: Re: JANUARY 2021 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello baydog! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It's great to see that after all of these years, you finally decided to make an account on-site. You'd be surprised at how many people remain lurkers forever - it's a real shame, considering that becoming ~one of us~ can not only let you vote, which also makes you able to affect the quality of works posted onsite, but also lets you comment and contribute. Speaking of which - it's great to see you want to do that. I can't wait to see what you'll come up with!

Without further ado though, let's click this collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Perplexing scenario about the past, and the future of SCP Series
item.content:encoded:
I'm a nobody, and haven't written in years (luckily for you because my writing for the past few years has been shit). However I've still followed, lightly, what's been going on with this community since 2015. I still find it strange, almost concerning that we're nearing Series VII, the SCP-6XXX series. It doesn't feel right, even Series III didn't feel right. Somehow, somewhere, deep down I feel as if post Series II (hell, maybe even Series I) doesn't feel right, natural, or believable. From simple stories about a vague entity studying creative takes on classic monsters and ideas, to esoteric gods and dimensions, back to an almost self-deprecating metaverse of irony.

I don't feel the sense of coherence, the idea that everything's under control, until when it's not. It seems as if everyone is vying for their chance to write the Next Big SCP Apocalypse Article! I want articles that expand our knowledge of the anomalous, the test logs, the interview logs, the recovery logs, what even is the Foundation as a part of our universe than just the aching backbone of a 70 year old man?

The culture of video games, movie shorts, RP servers, and pop Youtube has had its heavy mark on this community, down to the core. This is all my mere opinion, however. I haven't engaged heavily (and more often then not at all) here for years, and if someone could help me with this question. What the hell is going on, in the world these entities reside in?

item.title: Re: Recontainment Procedures.
item.content:encoded:
Hi there! Disclaimer I am not a veteran reviewer and I'm unable to provide Greenlights.

Lets take a look at this.
-

This is a pretty interesting concept, but I feel like some more details are needed.

A humanoid entity that recontains breached/breaching anomalies within its relevant location. Due to this, it is classified as a Thaumiel of sorts.

This could very well be a Thaumial, which is pretty cool, though I would like to know how the collector is able to contain the anomaly that it finds, and why. Keep in mind that writing a humanoid SCP is very difficult, because you will need to make sure that they are realistic and not just a shallow character.

The SCP is discovered after being sighted "collecting" multiple anomalies by a Foundation operative.

What kind of anomalies? What sort of things do they collect? Like I said before, you should expand on the details on the how and why the SCP does these things.

The SCP has another anomalous trait that is detailed in the draft that I made.

You should add this to the idea post then. You should explain the entirety of your idea so reviewers can have a good idea of what your plans for the article are. So far you have only used 156 out of the 400 word limit, so you have a lot of room to expand on the idea.

Over all this is a pretty interesting idea, and with the right execution could be very good. I would be curious to see how you plan on telling this story, and to learn more about the SCP. I suggest editing the post in order to give us a better idea of what is going on in this idea.

Hope this helped, and good luck.

item.title: Re: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
An artisan was selling some little plush creatures on her Etsy store. She took photos, and gave them a name, and wrote up a little backstory for them.

The original SCP-1926 was about those little plush creatures: it used the photos that the artisan had taken, and the name she had given them, and the backstory she had written. And it didn't credit her.

For the first few years of the Foundation project, we had a bad habit of grabbing weird pictures from wherever and basing SCPs on them without getting permission from the copyright owners. But that article wasn't just based on someone else's photo, it was based entirely on the story she'd written about them.

item.title: Re: Dimensional Snow
item.content:encoded:
Hi there! Disclaimer I am not a veteran reviewer and I'm unable to provide Greenlights.

Lets take a look at this.
-

Here are some areas of the idea that seemed problematic to me.

The foundation discovers the SCP in 1980 after a man commits suicide in his house via anomalous means.

Suicide is a very touchy subject. I don't recommend using this lightly, and if you do decide to use this, you should make sure that it makes sense in the narrative. Also you should elaborate on what "anomalous means" is. You should include all details that will be important to the narrative of the article so that reviewers will have a good understanding of what your article will be.

proven via use of SCP-507.

I don't think you should use 507 here. Your first article should stand on its own, so you should try and avoid leaning on other articles. Try and think of a different way of proving that the snowflakes contain pocket dimensions.

Any changes made to the dimension will change its represented snowflake and destruction of the snowflake will cause the destruction of its represented universe.

You should elaborate on what these changes would look like. I am also curious on how the Foundation would be able to witness these effects. Are they able to enter the snowflakes, or observe them in some other way?

So you have yourself a nice anomaly here, but you don't do very much with it. The most important part of an SCP is the narrative surrounding it, not the SCP itself. You should expand upon this idea, and edit your post above. You have only utilized 106 words of the 400 word limit, so you have a lot of room for adding details. Hope this helped. Good luck.

item.title: Re: Hearts and minds?
item.content:encoded:
Now, I know the obvious answer is no, they don't care about hearts and minds.

I feel like this is an oversimplification of the Foundation's worldview, honestly — they do have a strong sense of morality, but they're pathologically obsessed with injustices being done for the greater good. The atrocious acts you allude to aren't really done unthinkingly; presumably, someone at the top had to submit a request to the Ethics Committee, who weighed the risk and the reward and the necessity, and then gave the okay.

On an individual level, that's why you see personnel reacting so violently to things like Montauk, since they recognize the obvious inhumanity of it but also accept that their higher-ups have decided that it's for humanity's best. I imagine the same process would play out in your hypothetical retrieval mission, where it depends on someone in the chain of command weighing the risks and giving the order.

What you said is true and I did understand it wrong. I apologize for that. Still, why would the Foundation keep making that entity travel between other stories/realities? So it basically poses no threat at all, as long as people doesn't know his name and nobody plays as him. If the Foundation makes him go to another reality, like a story book, his name would be there, and now The Foundation would need to contain everything regarding that book. There are two options to contain this SCP: 1. Destroy everything regarding him and leave at least one thing about him inside one of the Foundation sites. Testing would always end up with amnestics, so it should be okay; 2. The Foundation creates a new story, either written, drawn or anything else, and make the entity go there. 1. Skips are supposed to use metric measurements; if imperial units are included at all, they should follow the metric units in parentheses. For instance: 2 meters (78 inches) long.

item.title: Dimensional Snow
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Each Snowflake produced represents a Dimension.

Central Narrative: The foundation discovers the SCP in 1980 after a man commit's suicide in his house. The foundation found a homemade snowflake experiment that produced snow via unknown means. Continued research produced the idea that each snowflake represented a single dimension which was proven via the foundations making major changes in other dimensions.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Each snowflake represents a single dimension and has been ever increasing since discovery. Any changes made to the dimension will change its represented snowflake and destruction of the snowflake will cause the destruction of its represented universe. The foundation is yet to discover how these snowflakes have connected the dimensions but have noticed that any interference from an outside source tends to change how much a snowflake looks like one another (If the foundation changes a Dimension, the snowflakes of each will highly resemble each other).

Additional Notes: Each snowflake represents its own version of reality and changes based on changes that occur in said dimension.
